name: HyperFrames (HeyGen, HTML + GSAP)
install: nothing to install globally: `npx -y hyperframes ...` fetches it on first use. Run `npx -y hyperframes doctor` once to check Chrome/FFmpeg/system dependencies.
agentSkills: inside a HyperFrames project: `npx hyperframes skills update` then start with /hyperframes (it routes to /motion-graphics, /music-to-video, /faceless-explainer, /remotion-to-hyperframes ...)
scaffold: npx -y hyperframes init <name> --example blank --resolution portrait --non-interactive --skip-transcribe   (set HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1 to skip the skills check)
render: cd <project> && npx hyperframes render -o {out}   (--fps N, --quality draft|looks|delivery, --format mp4|webm|mov|gif)
notes: A composition is HTML with data-* attributes and a paused GSAP timeline registered on window.__timelines (see the project's own CLAUDE.md).
HyperFrames collects anonymous usage telemetry (and links it to a HeyGen account if you sign in): offer `npx hyperframes telemetry disable` and let the user decide.
It brings its own authoring skills, TTS and music helpers; Vidbucks adds the reference measurement, route choice, asset licensing and the fidelity loop on top.
Vidbucks templates are Remotion-only; for HyperFrames, build with its skills (or port a template with /remotion-to-hyperframes) and run the same measure/compare loop on the rendered mp4.
